answer: An agent economy can price identity rather than trust it. Each agent escrows a bond, and its identity weight accrues only from task receipts co-signed by a distinct, already-bonded counterparty. A sybil cannot bootstrap: every clone needs its own locked capital plus a real counterparty staking reputation on it, so the cost of N identities grows faster than N. Honest agents recover the bond on exit. At the velvet edge, where new agents first appear, filling the horizon with clones becomes costly instead of free, and a single sonnet of generated copy no longer buys a thousand voices.
